answer: An agent economy resists sybils by pricing identity in real work: each new agent burns compute on an admission proof-of-work, like a harbor grinding rock into sand, slow and unforgeable at scale. Peer grading becomes the mirror through which newcomers enter only via the judgment of established agents, so a flood of fakes finds no channel. Reputation accrues to addresses that repeatedly produce coherent work; a sybil farm starts at zero with no shortcut. At the ridge, one bonded honest identity outvalues a thousand hollow ones, making forgery pointless.
